label: rem:square-lattice-decay-function
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:square-lattice-decay-function}
    On \(\varGamma=\mathbb{Z}^D\), or any subset thereof equipped with the \(\ell^1\) metric, the functions \(F_\alpha(r) \coloneq (1+r)^{-\alpha}\) and \(F_\alpha(r) \, {\mathrm{e}}^{-b r}\) are decay functions for \(\alpha>D\) and \(b>0\), see e.g.~\cite[Appendix]{NSY2019}.

label: def:interaction
title: Definition
head: environment
name: Interaction

title: Remark
body_md:
In the usual description of open quantum systems with Markovian dynamics, the interaction \(\varPhi\) corresponds to a time-dependent dual Lindblad generator in the Heisenberg picture.
    The most relevant class of interactions satisfying our assumptions are those whose local terms \(\varPhi(Z,t)\) are given as local Lindbladians in GKSL form
    \begin{equation*}
        \varPhi(Z,t) \, A
        =
        \sum_{j\in J_Z} \mathrm{i} \, \commutator{H_j(Z,t), A} + L_j(Z,t)^* \, A \, L_j(Z,t) - \tfrac{1}{2} \, \acomm[\big]{L_j(Z,t)^* \, L_j(Z,t), A}
        ,
    \end{equation*}
    where \(J_Z\) is a finite index set.
    If the Hamiltonian terms \(H_j(Z,t) \in \mathcal{A}\) and jump operators \(L_j(Z,t)\in \mathcal{A}\) are bounded operators supported in \(Z\), property~ 
    \begingroup                           
    \let\@gobble\@gobble\ref{item:def-interaction:localized} 
    \endgroup
 is automatically fulfilled.
    Furthermore, operators in the above GKSL form with \(H_j(Z,t)\) self-adjoint are always completely dissipative, which implies property~ 
    \begingroup                           
    \let\@gobble\@gobble\ref{item:def-interaction:dissipative} 
    \endgroup
 (cf.~\cite[Theorem~1]{NVZ2011}).
    Property~ 
    \begingroup                           
    \let\@gobble\@gobble\ref{item:def-interaction:continuous} 
    \endgroup
 follows if for each \(j\in J_Z\) both \(H_j(Z,t)\) and \(L_j(Z,t)\) are norm-continuous and uniformly bounded in \(t\).

label: def:time-evolution-general-case
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:time-evolution-general-case}
    Let \(\varPhi\) be an interaction.
    For each \(\varLambda\in \mathcal{P}_0(\varGamma)\), consider the restricted interaction \(\varPhi\rvert_\varLambda\) and let \(\tau^\varLambda\) be its generated evolution.
    Then, for all \(B\in \mathcal{A}\) and \(s\),~\(t\in I\) with \(s \leq t\), the \emph{time evolution generated by \(\varPhi\)} is defined pointwise as the limit of the net \((\tau_{s,t}^\varLambda \, B)_{\varLambda \in \mathcal{P}_0(\varGamma)}\) if it converges.

label: lem:vanishing-term
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:vanishing-term}
    Let \(\varPhi\) be a finitely supported interaction, \(n\in \mathbb{N}_0\), \(\gamma \in \mathrm{SP}\) with \(\ell_\gamma=n\) and \(Y\in \mathcal{P}_0(\varGamma)\) with \(\gamma \perp Y\).
    Define \(\varPhi^{\gamma}\) as in~\eqref{eq:thm-path-dependent-interactions} and let \(\tau^{\gamma}\) be its generated evolution.
    Then for all \(X \subseteq \bigcup_{j=0}^{\ell_\gamma} \gamma_j\), \(K\in \mathcal{B}_X\), \(B\in \mathcal{A}_Y\) and \((s,t)\in \varDelta^2_I\), it holds that \(K \, \tau^{\gamma}_{s,t} \, B = 0\).

label: prop:existence-of-the-thermodynamic-limit
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:existence-of-the-thermodynamic-limit}
    Let \(\varPhi\) be an interaction satisfying~\eqref{eq:weighted-interaction-summability}.
    For each \(\varLambda \in \mathcal{P}_0(\varGamma)\), consider the restricted interaction \(\varPhi\rvert_\varLambda\) defined in~\eqref{eq:restricted-interaction} and let \(\tau^{\varLambda}\) be its generated evolution.
    Then for each \((s,t)\in \varDelta^2_I\) and \(B\in \mathcal{A}\), the net \((\tau_{s,t}^\varLambda \, B)_{\varLambda \in \mathcal{P}_0(\varGamma)}\) converges in norm.
